portfolio.name: Fernwood Distribution Ltd, cloud portfolio (TEST SCENARIO)
purpose: Ranks five proposed cloud initiatives for a first funding tranche of up to 150,000 USD, weighted for run cost as the CFO instructed on 2026-03-02.
All names and figures are fictional test data.
Every score is a starting position for review, not a decision.

weight_rationale: Business outcome, not just technical change.
Highest weight: sponsor asked to reduce run cost first (LENS).
Second priority per sponsor: deadline risk.
Reduction in incidents and single points of failure.
Net change in security posture. Can be negative.

projects.name: Cloud cost visibility and tagging
projects.deadline: None. It is an enabler for P2, P3 and P4 savings claims.
projects.duration_note: 2 months, April to May 2026. R. Alder 120 hours.

business_value.assessment: Allocation of spend to a named owner moves from about 60% to 100%. It supports decisions but does not itself change the business outcome.

cost_optimization.assessment: No saving of its own, but it is the baseline that lets other savings be evidenced and booked. High value as an enabler.
cost_optimization.evidence: PROPOSAL-P1; COST_BASELINE shows P4 has no baseline.

time_criticality.assessment: No deadline and nothing gets worse monthly if it waits, but P2 and P3 savings cannot be proven until it lands.

risk_reduction.assessment: Little risk reduction. Untagged spend is a control weakness, not an incident source.

security_compliance.assessment: Neutral to slightly positive. Security review marked not required.

delivery_confidence.assessment: Small, well understood scope, two months, effort fits capacity.

dependencies: Shared services have no obvious owner. Needs a decision before enforcement.
120 hours in April and May. Check against P2 in the same months.
risks: Shared services have no tag owner, so spend stays unallocated
Name an owner per shared service before enforcement starts.
Monthly review in the infrastructure meeting.

projects.name: Retire the on-premises file servers
projects.deadline: 2027-01-31: Windows Server 2012 R2 extended support ends; insurer requires remediation by that date.
projects.basis: PROPOSAL-P2, ESTIMATE-P2, COST_BASELINE, INCIDENTS, CONTRACTS, SECURITY.
projects.duration_note: 4 months, April to July 2026. R. Alder 300 hours.

business_value.assessment: Removes recurring outages and an audit finding. The business outcome is reliability and compliance rather than new capability.

cost_optimization.assessment: Run cost 9,400 a month falls to 3,900 a month: 5,500 a month, about 66,000 a year, backed by the finance export.

time_criticality.assessment: Hard external date: OS support ends 2027-01-31 and the insurer requires remediation by then. Four months of work leaves margin.

risk_reduction.assessment: Removes the failing disk array behind three outages and closes the unsupported-OS audit finding.

security_compliance.assessment: Closes an open audit finding. Security review done with no objections.
security_compliance.evidence: SECURITY review status; INCIDENTS audit finding.

delivery_confidence.assessment: Pilot on the finance share ran four weeks with no issues. Cutover window for warehouse shares is still open.

strategic_alignment.assessment: Retires on-premises hardware, matching the target-state direction and principle 1.

dependencies: P1 gives the baseline against which the saving is shown. P2 can proceed without it but the saving is then asserted by finance export only.
300 hours across April to July, 75 a month.
Not agreed. Needed before cutover is scheduled.
risks: Data loss or permission errors at cutover
Parallel run with reconciliation of permissions and file counts before the old shares are switched off.
Agree the window with warehouse operations before scheduling.
OS support lapses before the migration completes
Four month plan ends July 2026, six months before the date. Escalate if cutover slips past October.

File service run cost per month

projects.name: Consolidate three monitoring tools
projects.deadline: 2026-09-16: notice date for tool C, which renews 2026-12-15 for 12 months at 2,700 a month.
projects.cost_note: ESTIMATE-P3. Line items sum to 72,000. Run cost after delivery varies with ingest.
projects.duration_note: 3 months, August to October 2026. R. Alder 120 hours.

business_value.assessment: One alerting path replaces three. Two missed alerts in six months show the cost of splitting them.

cost_optimization.assessment: Current spend 10,000 a month. After delivery 5,500 to 9,000 a month depending on ingest, so the saving is 1,000 to 4,500 a month, 12,000 to 54,000 a year. The vendor's 45% is the top of a range and is not used. Consumption billing and volume from P1 and P4 are not in the estimate.

time_criticality.assessment: Soft deadline: notice for tool C is due 2026-09-16 and the project ends in October, so renewal is likely unless the decision is made earlier.

risk_reduction.assessment: Fixes the missed-alert pattern but not the root cause of outages.

delivery_confidence.assessment: Moderate: new platform and billing model, R. Alder committed in the same months as P4 if P4 proceeds.

strategic_alignment.assessment: Implements target-state principle 3 and one observability platform.

dependencies: Ingest cost per team cannot be controlled without tagging.
risks: Ingest volume grows and the bill exceeds the estimate
Cap ingest per team, review monthly, set a budget alert.
Alert migration gaps during the switch
Run old and new in parallel for one on-call cycle.
kpis: Missed or one-tool-only alerts per 6 months
gates: Run owner after handover not named
Spend baseline known, ingest volume baseline not
Old tools kept until parallel run passes
Range of saving, not a point value; ingest not modelled
Data content of telemetry not classified
questions: What ingest volume should be assumed?
Is 2026-09-16 the decision date for tool C?

projects.name: Containerize order management on self-managed Kubernetes
projects.status: Proposed, not recommended in current form
projects.basis: PROPOSAL-P4, ESTIMATE-P4, TARGET_STATE, SECURITY, CAPACITY, COST_BASELINE.
projects.cost_note: ESTIMATE-P4 line items sum to 220,000. The proposal deck states 205,000, a 15,000 difference. 220,000 used.
projects.duration_note: 5 months, June to October 2026. R. Alder 1,100 hours.

business_value.assessment: Release lead time 14 to 5 days is a real benefit but unevidenced. The 14-day figure has no source. One rollback in the last six months.

cost_optimization.assessment: The claimed 30% run cost reduction has no baseline: the order-management platform is not in the finance export and ESTIMATE-P4 states no run cost. No saving can be claimed.

risk_reduction.assessment: Self-managed nodes add patching and cluster failure exposure. No incident history to remove.

security_compliance.assessment: Keys stored on nodes break SEC-07 and the managed-identity principle. Node patching moves from the provider to the platform team. Security review not started. Scored 1 until a design that meets SEC-07 exists.

delivery_confidence.assessment: R. Alder is estimated at 1,100 hours over 5 months against 160 productive hours a month (800 available), and the team has not run a production cluster.

strategic_alignment.assessment: Contradicts principle 1 (managed over self-managed) and direction to managed platform services.

dependencies: No baseline exists for order-management run cost. P1 would produce it.
Cluster telemetry would add ingest volume to a consumption-billed platform not in P3's estimate.
1,100 hours is more than available in the period and collides with P2 and P3.
risks: Credentials stored as keys on nodes breach SEC-07
Redesign to managed identity or drop the self-managed design.
Architect capacity exceeded: 1,100 hours against 800 available
Resequence, split the scope or reduce architect hours before approval.
Team has not run a production cluster
Managed Kubernetes service or training before approval.
gates: Run team after handover not agreed
Total in deck differs from line items by 15,000; run cost not stated
questions: What is the run cost baseline of the order-management platform?
Why does the deck total (205,000) differ from the line items (220,000)?
How will the design meet SEC-07?
How can 1,100 architect hours fit in the period?

P2.note: Current 9,400 a month falls to 3,900. 5,500 x 12 = 66,000.

P3.note: Conservative end of 1,000 to 4,500 a month. The vendor's 45% claim is not used.

P4.note: No baseline. No saving is claimed.

summary_notes: P2 ranks first on the run-cost lens: hard date, evidenced saving and the best case for a managed service. P1 has the best score per $100k and enables the others.
P4 scores lowest and should stay on hold: it breaches SEC-07, needs more architect hours than exist and has no cost baseline.
P5 is not scored. It has no business case or estimate.
